voiceover: You pull the latest code and your file is full of angle brackets, equal signs, and the word HEAD. That's a merge conflict. It sounds scary, but it just means two people changed the same line and git won't guess who's right. In a merge, the top half is your version and the bottom half is theirs. Pick one, or combine them, delete the markers, save, and commit. Git isn't broken. It's asking a question. Send this to whoever panics at merge conflicts.
